title: Quarterly Symphony: Hosted API + Model Catalog staffing, commit lanes, and risk grid
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: High-level quarterly plan to align Hosted API runway and model catalog curation into a coordinated delivery rhythm. This ticket captures the 'symphony' approach: define commit lanes, map OKRs to milestones, allocate staffing pods, enumerate gating criteria (quality/eval/rollback), and lay out a risk grid with mitigations. Goal is to produce a single master plan that program managers, platform engineering, model owners, and devrel can use as an execution contract for Q2 planning and early canary windows.
outcomes: 1) Clear commit lanes and owners for model rotations and hosted endpoint rollouts. 2) Mapped OKRs + leading indicators (latency, unit cost, model health, canary pass rate). 3) Staffing plan with cross-functional pods and backup coverage. 4) Risk grid + contingency playbooks for common failure modes (performance regressions, canary failures, region capacity constraints).
milestones: 2026-03-01: OKR metric targets and dashboards provisioned
2026-03-10: Complete model vetting checklist for first tranche
2026-03-17: Canary windows scheduled and runbooks drafted
commit_lanes: Core runtime improvements (latency/cost) - owner: Runtime Eng
Model curation & quantization profiles - owner: Model Ops
Hosted API UX/SDK/compatibility - owner: API PM/DevX
Canary & rollout automation - owner: Infra SRE/Deployments
okr_mapping: Primary OKR: Improve hosted inference economics and reliability. Key results targeted this quarter: decrease median p95 latency by 12%, reduce per-token cost on common workloads by 18% through batching/quantization defaults, maintain model-catalog health (no more than 1 regression per 50 deployments), and achieve 95% canary pass rate across tranches.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Each commit lane has a named owner and staffing pod with assigned engineers. 2) Dashboards for KR metrics exist and show baseline values. 3) At least one model rotation completed through canary with pre-defined rollback criteria. 4) Risk grid documented and runbooks linked. 5) Stakeholders sign off on release window and coverage plan.
risk_grid: Top risks: 1) Performance regression on long-context workloads - mitigation: extend canary to heavy-LLM traffic and add perf guardrails. 2) Capacity shortage in eu-west region - mitigation: pre-book Dedicated burst for affected customers and route noncritical traffic to compatible variants. 3) Model quality regression post-quantization - mitigation: holdback cohort and automated eval suite run for each candidate. 4) Docs/SDK mismatch causing adoption churn - mitigation: schedule DevX hotfix sprint and embargoed changelog cadence.
staffing_plan: Create 4 cross-functional pods (runtime, model-ops, API/DevX, SRE). Each pod: 2 engineers + 1 product lead + 1 QA/eval owner. Reserve 1 floater per pod for on-call overlap. Plan includes 20% capacity buffer for urgent rollbacks and incident response.
decision_gates: Gate A (design): commit lanes approved and owners assigned. Gate B (pre-canary): automated eval pass + perf regression < 3% vs baseline + docs updated. Gate C (release): canary pass rate >=95% and smoke checks green in two regions. Gate D (rollback): defined rollback window and verified fallback model variant.
notes: Workshop summary attached in Confluence; initial feedback from Runtime Eng favors prioritizing batching suggestions for small requests first to reduce tail latency. Model Ops flagged two models that need extra quantization QA. DevX requested an SDK deprecation window for older clients. Legal asked for audit logging notes for Private customers - low priority for hosted catalog but flagged for Private runway.
